mcat_description.short: Greenhouse Structure refers to prefabricated framed enclosures — primarily GI pipe or tubular steel frames covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film, polycarbonate sheets, or shade net — used for protected cultivation of horticultural crops in India. Sold as complete structure kits or turnkey installations, sized by covered area (sq mt).
mcat_description.long: Greenhouse structures in India are engineered prefabricated frames designed to create a controlled microclimate for year-round crop production, protecting plants from extreme weather, pests, and unseasonal rainfall. The dominant commercial form is the Naturally Ventilated Polyhouse (NVPH) — a hot-dip galvanised (HDG) GI pipe frame conforming to IS 1161 and IS 4759:2019, covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film of minimum 200 microns, compliant with IS 15827:2009 for film specifications and IS 14462:1997 for layout and structural design. Higher-specification variants include fan-and-pad (evaporative cooling) climate-controlled greenhouses and polycarbonate-covered structures for floriculture and tissue culture hardening. The Indian market is strongly shaped by NHB and MIDH government subsidy schemes, which mandate specific structural specifications (HDG pipe grade, zinc coating GSM, film micron thickness) and make subsidy compliance a primary purchase driver for farmer buyers.

market_context: In India, 'greenhouse structure' and 'polyhouse structure' are used interchangeably in trade, with 'polyhouse' being the dominant buyer vocabulary for agricultural protected cultivation structures. The market is strongly segmented by ventilation type: Naturally Ventilated Polyhouses (NVPH) dominate by volume, while Fan-and-Pad (evaporative cooling) greenhouses serve higher-value floriculture and export crops. The Bureau of Indian Standards has formulated IS 14462:1997 for layout, design, and construction of greenhouse structures, and IS 15827:2009 governs polyethylene film specifications; structural pipe standards follow IS 1161 (GI pipes) and IS 4759:2019 (hot-dip galvanisation at 275 GSM minimum). NHB (National Horticulture Board) and MIDH (Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture) subsidy compliance is a primary purchase driver — structures must meet prescribed HDG pipe thickness, zinc coating GSM, and UV film micron standards to qualify. Polycarbonate-covered greenhouses represent a premium segment used for floriculture, tissue culture hardening, and export-grade production. A secondary-hand market exists for used/dismantled polyhouse structures, particularly among small farmers (5–20 guntha plots). Key manufacturing hubs include Maharashtra (Pune), Gujarat, and Rajasthan.
